title: Nozik grammatik nuanslar va istisnolar
goal_uz: Dars oxirida inglizcha grammatikadagi nozik istisnolar va ma’no farqlarini (holat fe’llari, few/a few, remember to/-ing, variantlar) asoslab tushuntirasiz va sakkizta farqni qoida, ma’no hamda misol bilan izohlaysiz.

scenes.title: Nozik nuanslar darsiga xush kelibsiz
scenes.say_native: Assalomu alaykum! Oldingi darsda so‘z yasashning old va oxirgi qo‘shimchalarini chuqur ko‘rib chiqdik. Bugun grammatikaning eng nozik qatlamiga o‘tamiz: qoidalarning istisnolari, ma’noni deyarli sezdirmay o‘zgartiradigan kichik farqlar, ingliz tilida so‘zlashuvchilar orasidagi variantlar va ‘to‘g‘ri’ degan tushunchaning o‘zi. Dars oxirida sakkizta nozik farqni asoslab tushuntira olasiz.
scenes.say: Welcome to the final stretch of the grammar course. Today we look at the details that separate a very good speaker from a truly precise one: exceptions, shades of meaning, variation and the question of who decides what is correct.
scenes.say_uz: Grammatika kursining yakuniy bosqichiga xush kelibsiz. Bugun juda yaxshi so‘zlovchini haqiqatan aniq so‘zlovchidan ajratadigan tafsilotlarni ko‘ramiz: istisnolar, ma’no soyalari, variantlar va nima to‘g‘ri ekanini kim hal qilishi haqida.

scenes.title: Qoida — bu tendensiya
scenes.say_native: C2 darajasida qoidaga munosabat o‘zgaradi. Siz maktabda ‘bilish fe’llari davomiy shaklda ishlatilmaydi’ deb o‘rgangansiz. Bu to‘g‘ri, lekin faqat asosiy tendensiya. Istisnolarning ko‘pi tasodif emas, ularning ichida mantiq bor: ma’no o‘zgarsa, grammatika ham o‘zgaradi. Biz bugun har bir istisnoning ‘nima uchun’ ini topamiz, yodlab olmaymiz.
scenes.say: A rule is a strong tendency, not a law of nature. Most exceptions are not accidents. When the meaning changes, the grammar changes with it, and that is the logic we will look for.
scenes.say_uz: Qoida — kuchli tendensiya, tabiat qonuni emas. Istisnolarning ko‘pi tasodif emas. Ma’no o‘zgarsa, grammatika ham o‘zgaradi; biz shu mantiqni qidiramiz.

scenes.title: Holat fe’llari va davomiy shakl
board: He is being rude. (hozir shunday tutyapti)
scenes.say_native: Birinchi istisno: ‘be’ davomiy shaklda. ‘He is rude’ — uning xarakteri shunday. ‘He is being rude’ — u hozir, shu vaziyatda o‘zini shunday tutyapti, odatda esa unday emas. O‘zbekchada bunday farq bitta fe’l bilan berilmaydi, ‘o‘zini tutyapti’ deb tushuntirishga to‘g‘ri keladi. Ingliz tilida esa bitta -ing shu ma’noni beradi.
scenes.say: He is rude describes his character. He is being rude describes his behaviour right now, and it suggests that this is not typical for him.
scenes.say_uz: He is rude — uning xarakteri. He is being rude — hozirgi xatti-harakati, odatda bunday emasligini ham bildiradi.

scenes.title: Ikki ma’noli fe’llar
board: think: opinion → I think it's late
think: process → I'm thinking about it
see: understand → I see / meet → I'm seeing her
have: own → I have a car / experience → I'm having lunch

examples.t: I'm seeing the dentist at five.

scenes.say_native: Ikkinchi istisno: bir fe’lning ikki ma’nosi. ‘Think’ fikr bildirsa, davomiy bo‘lmaydi: ‘I think it’s late’. Lekin o‘ylash jarayoni bo‘lsa, bo‘ladi: ‘I’m thinking about it’. ‘See’ ‘tushunmoq’ bo‘lsa oddiy, ‘uchrashmoq’ bo‘lsa davomiy: ‘I’m seeing her tonight’. ‘Have’ ham shunday: ‘I have a car’, lekin ‘I’m having lunch’. Demak, qoida fe’lga emas, ma’noga tegishli.
scenes.say: Think, see and have can be stative or dynamic. I think it's late is an opinion. I'm thinking about it is a process. I see means I understand, but I'm seeing her tonight means a meeting.
scenes.say_uz: Think, see va have holat yoki harakat bo‘lishi mumkin. I think — fikr. I'm thinking — jarayon. I see — tushunaman; I'm seeing her — uchrashaman.

scenes.title: Haqiqiy xatolar
board: ✗ This book is belonging to me.
scenes.say_native: Endi istisno bilan xatoni adashtirmang. ‘Know’, ‘understand’, ‘belong’, ‘contain’, ‘consist’ kabi fe’llar deyarli har doim oddiy shaklda turadi. O‘zbek tilida ‘bilib turibman’ yoki ‘tegishli bo‘lib turibdi’ deyish mumkin bo‘lgani uchun, ko‘p kishi ‘I am knowing’ deb xato qiladi. Bu yerda istisno yo‘q: ma’no o‘zgarmaydi, demak shakl ham o‘zgarmaydi.
scenes.say: Do not confuse a real exception with a real mistake. Know, understand, belong and contain almost never take the continuous form. I know the answer. This book belongs to me.
scenes.say_uz: Haqiqiy istisnoni haqiqiy xato bilan aralashtirmang. Know, understand, belong, contain deyarli hech qachon davomiy bo‘lmaydi.

scenes.title: To‘g‘ri shaklni tanlang
board: 3) I ___ the dentist at five. (see/am seeing)
4) This house ___ to my aunt. (belongs/is belonging)
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta gap. Har birida bo‘sh joyga qaysi shakl mos kelishini o‘ylang va ovoz chiqarib butun gapni ayting. Birinchida odatdagi xulq emas, vaqtinchalik holat haqida gap ketyapti.
scenes.say: One. He blank difficult today, but he is usually very pleasant. Two. I blank it contains garlic. Three. I blank the dentist at five tomorrow. Four. This house blank to my aunt.
scenes.say_uz: Bir. U bugun qiyin, odatda esa juda yoqimli. Ikki. Menimcha, unda sarimsoq bor. Uch. Ertaga beshda tish shifokoriga boraman. To‘rt. Bu uy xolamniki.

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: 3) I'm seeing the dentist at five.
4) This house belongs to my aunt.
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Bir: ‘is being’, chunki odatdagidan farqli vaqtinchalik xulq. Ikki: ‘I think’, chunki bu fikr, jarayon emas. Uch: ‘I’m seeing’, chunki rejalashtirilgan uchrashuv. To‘rt: ‘belongs’, chunki ‘belong’ hech qachon davomiy bo‘lmaydi. Agar uchtasini to‘g‘ri topgan bo‘lsangiz, ma’noga qarab qaror qilish odatini egallayapsiz.
scenes.say: One: is being. Two: I think. Three: I'm seeing. Four: belongs. Always decide by meaning, not by the verb alone.
scenes.say_uz: Bir: is being. Ikki: I think. Uch: I'm seeing. To‘rt: belongs. Har doim fe’lga emas, ma’noga qarab qaror qiling.

scenes.title: Birlik shaklidagi ‘ko‘plik’ otlar
scenes.say_native: Ikkinchi istisnolar guruhi — son. ‘News’ ko‘plik ‘s’ bilan tugasa ham birlik: ‘The news is bad’. ‘Mathematics’ va ‘physics’ ham shunday. ‘Police’ esa aksincha, ‘s’ siz tugasa ham ko‘plik: ‘The police are here’. ‘Scissors’, ‘trousers’, ‘glasses’ faqat ko‘plikda, bitta narsa uchun ‘a pair of’ deymiz. O‘zbekchada ‘yangilik’ va ‘xabar’ ko‘pincha ko‘plikda keladi, shuning uchun adashasiz.
scenes.say: News is singular even though it ends in s: the news is bad. Police is plural without an s: the police are here. Scissors and trousers are plural only, so we say a pair of scissors.
scenes.say_uz: News s bilan tugasa ham birlik. Police s siz ko‘plik. Scissors va trousers faqat ko‘plikda, shuning uchun a pair of deymiz.

scenes.title: Sanalmaydigan va ko‘plik otlar
board: ✓ Some information / a piece of advice
✗ The police is here. ✓ The police are here.
scenes.say_native: Eng ko‘p uchraydigan uchta xato. ‘Information’ va ‘advice’ sanalmaydigan ot, ularga ‘s’ qo‘shilmaydi. Bittasini aytmoqchi bo‘lsangiz, ‘a piece of advice’ yoki ‘a piece of information’ deysiz. ‘The news are’ ham xato. Ammo ‘data’ haqida keyinroq gaplashamiz, chunki u yerda istisno emas, haqiqiy tortishuv bor: zamonaviy tilda ‘The data is’ ham, ‘The data are’ ham uchraydi.
scenes.say: Information and advice are uncountable: some information, a piece of advice. The news is bad, and the police are here. Data is a more interesting case that we will return to.
scenes.say_uz: Information va advice sanalmaydi: some information, a piece of advice. The news is bad; the police are here. Data esa qiziqarli holat, unga qaytamiz.

scenes.title: Artikl istisnolari: muassasalar
board: BrE: in hospital  |  AmE: in the hospital

examples.t: She is at university in Leeds.
I went to the school to speak to the head.
examples.uz: Men direktor bilan gaplashgani maktabga bordim.

scenes.say_native: Artikl qoidasining ajoyib istisnosi: muassasalar. ‘School’, ‘hospital’, ‘university’, ‘prison’, ‘church’ — agar ularning asl vazifasi nazarda tutilsa, artiklsiz keladi. ‘She is at university’ — u talaba. Lekin binaning o‘ziga borsangiz, ‘the’ kerak: ‘I went to the school to see the head’. Britaniya ingliz tilida ‘in hospital’ deyiladi, Amerikada esa odatda ‘in the hospital’. Bu variantga keyinroq qaytamiz.
scenes.say: With institutions we drop the article when we mean their purpose. She is at university means she is a student. But I went to the school to see the head means the building. British English says in hospital; American English usually says in the hospital.
scenes.say_uz: Muassasalar vazifasi nazarda tutilsa artiklsiz keladi. She is at university — u talaba. Binaning o‘zi bo‘lsa the kerak. Britaniyada in hospital, Amerikada odatda in the hospital.

scenes.title: Qiyoslash darajasi: ikki yo‘l

examples.t: It's a quieter street than mine.

scenes.say_native: Qiyoslashda oddiy qoida: bir bo‘g‘inli sifatga ‘-er’, uzun sifatga ‘more’. Lekin ikki bo‘g‘inli sifatlarning katta guruhida ikkala shakl ham to‘g‘ri: ‘quiet’, ‘clever’, ‘narrow’, ‘simple’, ‘polite’, ‘common’. Ikkalasini ham ishlatsangiz bo‘ladi, ‘-er’ shakli biroz ixchamroq va ko‘proq yozma nutqqa xos eshitiladi. Uch va undan ko‘p bo‘g‘inlida esa ‘more’ qoladi.
scenes.say: The comparative rule has a grey zone. Many two-syllable adjectives, like quiet, clever, narrow and common, accept both forms. Longer adjectives keep more: more beautiful, never beautifuler.
scenes.say_uz: Ikki bo‘g‘inli ko‘p sifatlarda ikkala shakl to‘g‘ri: quieter yoki more quiet. Uzun sifatlarda faqat more.

scenes.title: Fe’l ortidan to‘ldiruvchi: ma’no almashadi
board: try to → harakat qilmoq  |  try -ing → sinab ko‘rmoq

examples.t: I remembered to lock the door.

scenes.say_native: Endi ma’no nozikliklariga o‘tamiz. Ba’zi fe’llardan keyin ‘to’ va ‘-ing’ butunlay boshqa ma’no beradi. ‘Remember to lock’ — qulflashni esdan chiqarmadim. ‘Remember locking’ — qulflaganimni xotiramda saqlayman. ‘Stop to rest’ — dam olish uchun to‘xtadim. ‘Stop resting’ — dam olishni to‘xtatdim. ‘Try to open’ — ochishga urindim, ‘try opening’ — usul sifatida ochib ko‘rdim.
scenes.say: Some verbs change meaning with the form that follows. Remember to lock is a duty done. Remember locking is a memory of the action. Stop to rest gives a reason. Stop resting ends the activity. Try to open is an effort; try opening is an experiment.
scenes.say_uz: Ba’zi fe’llarda keyingi shakl ma’noni o‘zgartiradi: remember to — vazifa; remember -ing — xotira; stop to — maqsad; stop -ing — tugatish; try to — urinish; try -ing — sinab ko‘rish.

scenes.title: Bir juft, ikki ma’no
board: I regret to tell you… (afsus bilan xabar qilaman)

examples.uz: Uni birinchi marta ko‘rganimni hech unutmayman.

scenes.say_native: Yana ikkita juft. ‘Forget to post’ — xatni yuborish esdan chiqdi, demak xat hali jo‘natilmagan. ‘Forget posting’ — yuborgan edim, lekin buni unutdim. ‘Regret to tell you’ — rasmiy xabar boshlanishi: afsuski, aytishga to‘g‘ri keladi. ‘Regret telling you’ — aytib qo‘ygan bo‘lsangiz va pushaymon bo‘lsangiz. Rasmiy xatlarda birinchisini ko‘p uchratasiz.
scenes.say: I forgot to post it means the letter is still here. I forgot posting it means I did it but cannot recall. I regret to tell you is formal news. I regret telling you means I wish I had stayed silent.
scenes.say_uz: Forgot to post — xat hali yuborilmagan. Forgot posting — yuborilgan, lekin esda yo‘q. Regret to tell you — rasmiy xabar. Regret telling you — aytganimga pushaymonman.

scenes.title: Qaysi ma’no?
board: 1) He stopped to talk to her.
scenes.say_native: Har bir gap uchun o‘zbekcha ma’nosini ayting va bajarilgan harakat bor-yo‘qligini aniqlang. Birinchi va ikkinchi gapni solishtiring: ularning birida u gapirish uchun to‘xtagan, ikkinchisida esa gapirishni to‘xtatgan. Uchinchi va to‘rtinchida nima haqida aytilyapti?
scenes.say: One: He stopped to talk to her. Two: He stopped talking to her. Three: Try pressing the red button. Four: I remember sending the file.
scenes.say_uz: Bir: U u bilan gaplashish uchun to‘xtadi. Ikki: U u bilan gaplashishni to‘xtatdi. Uch: Qizil tugmani bosib ko‘ring. To‘rt: Faylni yuborganim esimda.

scenes.title: Javoblar
scenes.say_native: Birinchi gap: u yo‘lda to‘xtab, u bilan gaplashmoqchi. Ikkinchi gap: gap-so‘z tugadi, aloqa uzildi. Uchinchi gap: bu buyruq emas, maslahat: ‘bosib ko‘ring, balki ishlar’. To‘rtinchi gap: fayl allaqachon yuborilgan va bu esimda. E’tibor bering: ‘to’ li shakl maqsad va kelajakka, ‘-ing’ li shakl esa jarayon va o‘tmishga qaraydi.
scenes.say: One: he paused in order to talk to her. Two: he ended the conversation. Three: it is a suggestion to experiment. Four: the file has already been sent. The to form looks forward, the -ing form looks at the activity or the past.
scenes.say_uz: Bir: gaplashish uchun to‘xtadi. Ikki: gaplashishni tugatdi. Uch: sinab ko‘rish maslahati. To‘rt: fayl allaqachon yuborilgan. To-shakl oldinga, -ing shakl jarayon yoki o‘tmishga qaraydi.

scenes.title: Few va a few, little va a little
board: a few / a little → bir oz bor (ijobiy)

examples.t: Few people came, so we cancelled.
examples.uz: Deyarli hech kim kelmadi, shuning uchun bekor qildik.

examples.t: A few people came, so we started.
examples.uz: Bir necha kishi keldi, shuning uchun boshladik.

scenes.say_native: Faqat bitta ‘a’ harfi ma’noni teskari qiladi. ‘Few people came’ — deyarli hech kim kelmadi, bu salbiy ohang. ‘A few people came’ — bir necha kishi keldi, bu ijobiy. ‘Little hope’ — umid deyarli yo‘q. ‘A little hope’ — oz bo‘lsa-da umid bor. O‘zbekchada ‘oz’ so‘zi ikkala holni qoplaydi, shuning uchun ohangni ingliz tilida ataylab tanlash kerak. ‘Quite a few’ esa ‘ancha ko‘p’ degani.
scenes.say: One small word reverses the mood. Few people came means almost nobody. A few people came means some did, which is positive. Little hope is nearly none; a little hope is something to hold on to. Quite a few means a fair number.
scenes.say_uz: Bitta a ma’noni teskari qiladi. Few — deyarli hech kim, a few — bir necha. Little hope — umid yo‘q, a little hope — oz bo‘lsa-da umid bor. Quite a few — ancha ko‘p.

scenes.title: Only — joyi ma’noni o‘zgartiradi
board: Only I saw him. (boshqa hech kim)
I saw only him. (boshqa hech kimni)

examples.uz: Anna menga faqat qarz berdi, sovg‘a qilmadi.

scenes.say_native: ‘Only’ so‘zi so‘zlashuvda ko‘pincha fe’l oldiga qo‘yiladi, lekin aniq ma’no uchun u ta’sir qilayotgan so‘zning yoniga turishi kerak. ‘Only Anna lent me money’ — boshqa hech kim bermagan. ‘Anna only lent me money’ — Anna pul qarz berdi, sovg‘a qilmadi. Yozma nutqda, ayniqsa bahsli joylarda, ‘only’ ni to‘g‘ri joyga qo‘ying. Og‘zaki nutqda esa ohang ko‘pincha chalkashlikni bartaraf etadi.
scenes.say: The word only should sit next to what it limits. Only Anna lent me money means nobody else did. Anna only lent me money means she lent it, not gave it. In speech, intonation usually repairs the ambiguity; in writing, placement matters.
scenes.say_uz: Only ta’sir qilayotgan so‘zning yonida turishi kerak. Only Anna — boshqa hech kim emas. Anna only lent — qarz berdi, sovg‘a emas. Og‘zaki nutqda ohang yordam beradi.

scenes.title: Urg‘u ma’noni o‘zgartiradi
board: I didn't SAY he stole it. (lekin ishora qilgandim)
I didn't say HE stole it. (boshqa kishi)
I didn't say he STOLE it. (ehtimol qarz olgan)

examples.t: I didn't say HE stole the money.
I didn't say he STOLE the money.

scenes.say_native: Ingliz tilida bitta gapning ma’nosi faqat urg‘u bilan o‘zgaradi. Gapdagi har bir so‘z urg‘u olishi mumkin, va urg‘u olgan so‘z ‘aynan shu, boshqasi emas’ degan ishorani beradi. ‘I didn't say HE stole it’ — pulni boshqa kishi o‘g‘irlagan bo‘lishi mumkin. ‘I didn't say he STOLE it’ — balki qarz olgandir. O‘zbek tilida buni so‘z tartibi va ‘-ku’, ‘-mi’ yuklamalari bilan beramiz.
scenes.say: The same sentence can carry different meanings depending on which word you stress. I didn't say HE stole it suggests someone else did. I didn't say he STOLE it suggests he did something else with it. Stress points to a contrast.
scenes.say_uz: Bir xil gap urg‘uga qarab turli ma’no beradi. Urg‘u olgan so‘z qarama-qarshilikni ko‘rsatadi: I didn't say HE stole it — boshqa kishi o‘g‘irlagan bo‘lishi mumkin.

scenes.title: Urg‘uni toping
board: A: Did you say she lied?
B: I didn't say SHE lied. →  ?
B: I didn't say she LIED. →  ?
scenes.say_native: Ikkita javobni o‘qing va har birida urg‘u berilgan so‘zni baland ovozda kuchaytiring. Keyin ma’nosini ayting: birinchisida kim yolg‘on gapirgan bo‘lishi mumkin, ikkinchisida u nima qilgan bo‘lishi mumkin? Javobni o‘zbekcha ayting.
scenes.say: I didn't say SHE lied. I didn't say she LIED. Say both aloud, stressing the capital word. What does each one suggest?
scenes.say_uz: Men u yolg‘on gapirdi, demadim. Men u yolg‘on gapirdi, demadim. Ikkalasini ham baland ovozda ayting. Har biri nimani anglatadi?

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: LIED → u noto‘g‘ri gapirgan, lekin qasddan emas
scenes.say_native: Birinchi javob: ‘SHE’ ga urg‘u bersangiz, yolg‘onchi boshqa odam, ehtimol uning do‘sti. Ikkinchi javob: ‘LIED’ ga urg‘u bersangiz, u xato qilgan, adashgan yoki bo‘rttirgan bo‘lishi mumkin, lekin qasddan yolg‘on gapirmagan. Siz endi gapning ma’nosi faqat grammatikada emas, ritm va urg‘uda ham borligini his qildingiz. Bu C2 darajasining belgilaridan biri.
scenes.say: With stress on SHE, the liar was somebody else. With stress on LIED, she may have been mistaken or exaggerated but did not deliberately lie. Meaning lives in rhythm as well as in grammar.
scenes.say_uz: SHE ga urg‘u — yolg‘onchi boshqa odam. LIED ga urg‘u — u adashgan, lekin qasddan yolg‘on gapirmagan. Ma’no ritmda ham yashaydi.

scenes.title: Present perfect va o‘tgan zamon nuansi
board: I've lost my keys. (hozir ham yo‘q)
I lost my keys. (voqea, natija noma’lum)
She has been to Paris. (borib kelgan)
She has gone to Paris. (hozir u yerda)

examples.uz: U Rimga ketgan, hozir u yerda.

scenes.say_native: Present perfect o‘tgan harakatni hozirgi holat bilan bog‘laydi. ‘I’ve lost my keys’ — kalitlar hozir ham yo‘q. ‘I lost my keys’ — o‘tmishdagi voqea, ular topilgan bo‘lishi ham mumkin. Eng nozik juft: ‘has been to’ — borib qaytgan, ‘has gone to’ — hozir o‘sha yerda. O‘zbekchada ‘borgan’ so‘zi ikkalasini ham qoplaydi, shuning uchun ingliz tilida bu farqni alohida eslab qoling.
scenes.say: Present perfect links the past to the present. I've lost my keys means they are still missing. I lost my keys just reports an event. And has been to means she visited and came back, whereas has gone to means she is there now.
scenes.say_uz: Present perfect o‘tmishni hozirga bog‘laydi. I've lost — kalitlar hozir ham yo‘q. Has been to — borib qaytgan; has gone to — hozir o‘sha yerda.

scenes.title: Hisobot muharririda
board: Writer: Few figures are missing, but I've sent a few.
Editor: I'm seeing the client at four.
Writer: Then I only need a little time.
scenes.say_native: Endi dialogni tinglang. Muharrir va muallif hisobot ustida ishlashyapti. Muallif ‘few’ va ‘a few’ ni, ‘a little’ ni ataylab tanlaydi, muharrir esa uchrashuvga shoshilyapti. Tinglayotganda ikkita narsani toping: qaysi raqamlar yetishmayapti, va yuborilgan raqamlar bormi?
scenes.say: Editor: Is the report ready? I'm seeing the client at four. Writer: Nearly. Few figures are still missing, but I've already sent you a few. Editor: Which ones? Writer: The ones for March. I only need a little time for the rest. Editor: You have an hour. I think that's enough.
scenes.say_uz: Muharrir: Hisobot tayyormi? Soat to‘rtda mijoz bilan uchrashaman. Muallif: Deyarli. Ba’zi raqamlar yetishmaydi, lekin bir nechtasini yubordim. Muharrir: Qaysilarini? Muallif: Mart uchun. Qolganiga ozgina vaqt kerak. Muharrir: Bir soatingiz bor. Menimcha, yetadi.

scenes.title: Dialogni tushundingizmi?
board: 1) When does the editor meet the client?
2) Has the writer sent anything yet?
3) How much time does the writer ask for?
scenes.say_native: Uchta savolga o‘zbekcha yoki inglizcha javob bering. Birinchi: muharrir mijoz bilan soat nechada uchrashadi? Ikkinchi: muallif biror narsa yuborganmi? Uchinchi: muallif qancha vaqt so‘raydi va ‘a little’ ning ohangi qanday? Kerak bo‘lsa, dialogni yana eslang.
scenes.say: One: When does the editor meet the client? Two: Has the writer sent anything yet? Three: How much time does the writer need?
scenes.say_uz: Bir: Muharrir mijoz bilan qachon uchrashadi? Ikki: Muallif biror narsa yuborganmi? Uch: Muallifga qancha vaqt kerak?

scenes.title: Dialog javoblari
board: 2) Yes — a few figures, for March
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Birinchi: soat to‘rtda, ‘I’m seeing the client’ — rejalashtirilgan uchrashuv. Ikkinchi: ha, muallif bir nechta raqamni, Mart uchun bo‘lganlarini yuborgan: ‘a few’ ijobiy. Uchinchi: ‘a little time’ — ozgina vaqt, ohangi ijobiy: ish deyarli tayyor. Agar muallif ‘little time’ degan bo‘lsa, vaqt deyarli yo‘q, degan ma’no chiqardi va muharrir xavotirga tushardi.
scenes.say: One: at four, a planned meeting. Two: yes, a few figures for March. Three: a little time, which sounds positive. If the writer had said little time, the editor would have worried.
scenes.say_uz: Bir: soat to‘rtda. Ikki: ha, Mart uchun bir nechta raqam. Uch: a little time, ijobiy ohang. Little time desa, muharrir xavotirga tushardi.

scenes.title: Jamoaviy otlar: Britaniya va Amerika
board: BrE: The team are winning. / The team is winning.
the government, the band, the committee
scenes.say_native: Endi variantlarga o‘tamiz. Jamoaviy otlar — ‘team’, ‘government’, ‘committee’, ‘band’. Britaniya ingliz tilida ularni ko‘plik fe’li bilan ishlatish mumkin, agar a’zolarni alohida odamlar sifatida ko‘rsangiz: ‘The team are arguing’. Birlik ham to‘g‘ri. Amerika ingliz tilida odatda faqat birlik: ‘The team is winning’. Ikkala shakl ham to‘g‘ri, faqat bir gap ichida ularni aralashtirmaslik muhim.
scenes.say: Collective nouns like team, government and committee can take a plural verb in British English when we think of the individual members. American English normally uses the singular. Both are fine; just stay consistent within a sentence.
scenes.say_uz: Team, government, committee kabi otlar Britaniya ingliz tilida a’zolarga e’tibor berilsa ko‘plik fe’li oladi. Amerikada odatda birlik. Ikkalasi ham to‘g‘ri, faqat izchil bo‘ling.

scenes.title: Kundalik variantlar
board: BrE: I've got / have got  |  AmE: I have / I've gotten
at the weekend (BrE)  |  on the weekend (AmE)
scenes.say_native: Bir nechta farq yodingizda tursin. Amerika ingliz tilida ‘gotten’ — ‘bo‘lib qoldi, oldi’ ma’nosida: ‘She has gotten better’. Britaniyada ‘got’ ishlatiladi. ‘Learnt’ va ‘learned’ ikkalasi Britaniyada bor, Amerikada ‘learned’. ‘Dived’ Britaniyada, ‘dove’ Amerikada keng tarqalgan. ‘At the weekend’ Britaniyaga, ‘on the weekend’ Amerikaga xos. ‘Different from’ hamma joyda, ‘different to’ Britaniyada, ‘different than’ Amerikada uchraydi.
scenes.say: Some everyday differences: Americans say has gotten, British speakers say has got. Learnt and learned both exist in Britain. Dived is British, dove is American. At the weekend is British, on the weekend is American. Different from works everywhere.
scenes.say_uz: Americans: has gotten; British: has got. Learnt va learned Britaniyada ikkalasi ham bor. Dived — Britaniya, dove — Amerika. At the weekend — Britaniya, on the weekend — Amerika. Different from hamma joyda ishlaydi.

scenes.title: Subjunktiv va singular they
board: AmE: I suggest that he go. | BrE: …that he should go.
singular they: Someone left their bag.

examples.t: If I were you, I'd apologise.

scenes.say_native: Yana ikkita mavzu. Birinchisi — shart gaplarda ‘were’: ‘If I were you’. Bu standart va rasmiy shakl, kundalik nutqda ‘If I was you’ ham uchraydi. Maslahat berishdan keyin Amerikada ‘I suggest that he go’, Britaniyada ‘that he should go’. Ikkinchisi — birlik ‘they’: ‘Someone left their bag’. U asrlar davomida ishlatiladi va bugun standart deb qabul qilingan, shuning uchun ‘his or her’ dan ko‘ra tabiiyroq eshitiladi.
scenes.say: If I were you is the standard form, though many speakers say if I was you. After suggest, American English prefers the bare form, he go, while British English adds should. And singular they, as in someone left their bag, has been used for centuries and is fully standard today.
scenes.say_uz: If I were you — standart shakl, kundalikda if I was you ham bor. Suggest dan keyin Amerikada he go, Britaniyada should go. Birlik they asrlar davomida ishlatiladi va bugun standart.

scenes.title: Giperkorrektsiya tuzog‘i
board: ✗ He gave it to John and I.
✓ He gave it to John and me.
scenes.say_native: Bu yerda qiziq hodisa bor: giperkorrektsiya. Bolaligida ‘Me and John went’ deb xato qilgan va tuzatilgan odam keyin har joyda ‘and I’ deydi, hatto kerak bo‘lmagan joyda ham. Predlogdan keyin hamma vaqt ‘me’ keladi: ‘between you and me’. Tekshirish usuli oddiy: ‘and John’ ni olib tashlang. ‘He gave it to I’ deb bo‘lmaydi, demak ‘He gave it to me’. Rasmiy ko‘rinish uchun ishlatilgan ‘I’ aslida noto‘g‘ri.
scenes.say: A famous trap is hypercorrection. Speakers who were once corrected for me and John went start saying and I everywhere. After a preposition we need me: between you and me. Remove the other person to test it: he gave it to me, not to I.
scenes.say_uz: Giperkorrektsiya: har joyda and I deyish. Predlogdan keyin me kerak: between you and me. Tekshirish: boshqa shaxsni olib tashlang, he gave it to me.

scenes.title: Britaniyami yoki Amerikami?
board: 2) The team are playing well tonight.
3) We went out at the weekend.
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta gap. Har birini eshitib, ular qaysi variantga xosligini ayting: Britaniya, Amerika yoki ikkalasiga ham mumkinmi. To‘rtinchi gapda fe’lning o‘tgan zamon shakliga e’tibor bering.
scenes.say: One: She has gotten much better. Two: The team are playing well tonight. Three: We went out at the weekend. Four: He dove into the lake.
scenes.say_uz: Bir: U ancha yaxshilandi. Ikki: Jamoa bugun yaxshi o‘ynayapti. Uch: Biz dam olish kunlari chiqdik. To‘rt: U ko‘lga sho‘ng‘idi.

scenes.title: Variant javoblari
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Birinchi gap — Amerika, chunki ‘gotten’. Ikkinchi — Britaniya, jamoaga ko‘plik fe’li. Uchinchi — Britaniya, ‘at the weekend’. To‘rtinchi — Amerika, ‘dove’. Muhim narsa: bu farqlarni yodlab olish emas, ularni tanib olish va bir matn ichida izchil saqlash. Siz o‘z variantingizni tanlab, unga sodiq qolsangiz, nutqingiz professional ko‘rinadi.
scenes.say: One: American, gotten. Two: British, plural verb. Three: British, at the weekend. Four: American, dove. The skill is not memorising two lists but recognising a variety and staying consistent in your own writing.
scenes.say_uz: Bir: Amerika. Ikki: Britaniya. Uch: Britaniya. To‘rt: Amerika. Asosiysi — variantni tanib olish va o‘z matningizda izchil bo‘lish.

scenes.title: Preskriptiv va deskriptiv
board: Prescriptive: how language SHOULD be used
Both are useful — for different jobs
scenes.say_native: Endi eng falsafiy savol: ‘to‘g‘ri’ ni kim hal qiladi? Preskriptiv yondashuv til qanday bo‘lishi kerakligini aytadi: qoidalar, uslub qo‘llanmalari. Deskriptiv yondashuv esa odamlar haqiqatda qanday gapirishini kuzatadi va yozib boradi. Lug‘atchilar asosan deskriptiv ishlaydi. Muharrirlar va imtihon tuzuvchilar esa ko‘pincha preskriptiv. Ikkalasi ham foydali, faqat turli vazifalar uchun.
scenes.say: Prescriptive grammar says how language should be used. Descriptive grammar records how it actually is used. Dictionary makers mostly describe; style guides and examiners often prescribe. Both have a job to do.
scenes.say_uz: Preskriptiv grammatika til qanday bo‘lishi kerakligini aytadi, deskriptiv esa haqiqatda qanday ishlatilishini yozadi. Ikkalasi ham foydali.

scenes.title: Mashhur ‘qoidalar’ tortishuvi
board: Who are you talking to? — end preposition
And / But at the start of a sentence
fewer people / less people · The data is / are

examples.t: We need to seriously consider it.
examples.uz: Biz buni jiddiy ko‘rib chiqishimiz kerak.

examples.t: Who did you give it to?

scenes.say_native: Mana bir nechta mashhur ‘qoida’. Birinchi, ‘to’ va fe’l orasiga ravish qo‘ymang: ‘to boldly go’ — ayrilgan infinitiv. Bu qoida lotin tilidan nusxa olingan, ingliz tilida esa infinitiv ikki so‘z. Ikkinchi, gapni predlog bilan tugatmang. Uchinchi, gapni ‘And’ yoki ‘But’ bilan boshlamang. To‘rtinchi, ‘fewer’ sanaladigan narsa uchun, ‘less’ sanalmaydigan uchun. Zamonaviy ingliz tilida bu qoidalarning ko‘pi qat’iy emas, lekin rasmiy matnda ba’zan talab qilinadi.
scenes.say: Some famous rules are worth a second look. Do not split an infinitive: to boldly go. Do not end with a preposition. Do not begin with and or but. Use fewer with countable nouns. Many are only conventions, but some editors and examiners still expect them in formal writing.
scenes.say_uz: Mashhur qoidalar: infinitivni ajratmang, gapni predlog bilan tugatmang, And/But bilan boshlamang, fewer sanaladigan otlar bilan. Ko‘pi qat’iy emas, lekin rasmiy yozuvda ba’zan talab qilinadi.

scenes.title: Qaror qabul qilish usuli
board: 3) What do dictionaries and corpora show?
scenes.say_native: Shubhali holatda to‘rtta savol bering. Birinchi, o‘quvchi yoki tinglovchi kim? Imtihon ekspertimi yoki do‘stmi? Ikkinchi, vaziyat qanchalik rasmiy? Uchinchi, lug‘atlar va til korpuslari, masalan Cambridge, Oxford yoki Collins, bu shaklni qanday baholaydi? To‘rtinchi, matn ichida izchillikni saqlayapsizmi? Shunday qilib, ‘to‘g‘ri’ degan mutlaq so‘z o‘rniga ‘shu vaziyatda o‘rinli’ deb o‘ylashni o‘rganasiz.
scenes.say: When in doubt, ask four questions. Who is my reader? How formal is the situation? What do reputable dictionaries and corpora show? And am I being consistent? Appropriate usually beats absolutely correct.
scenes.say_uz: Shubhada to‘rt savol: o‘quvchi kim, vaziyat qanchalik rasmiy, lug‘atlar nima deydi, matn izchilmi? Mutlaq to‘g‘ri o‘rniga o‘rinli deb o‘ylang.

scenes.title: Muharrir va yozuvchi
board: Editor: You split the infinitive here.
Writer: To fully understand it is clearer.
Editor: For the journal, rephrase it.
Writer: Fine. Fewer words, same meaning.
scenes.say_native: Ikkinchi dialogni tinglang. Jurnal muharriri maqolada ayrilgan infinitivni topdi. Yozuvchi esa aniqlik uchun uni saqlamoqchi. Ular qaysi qaror bilan kelishishadi va nima uchun? Muharrirning dalili qoidaning to‘g‘riligida emas, boshqa narsada. Nimada ekanini toping.
scenes.say: Editor: You have split the infinitive in line three. Writer: To fully understand the result is actually clearer. Editor: I agree it is not wrong. But the journal's house style avoids it, so please rephrase. Writer: Fair enough. I'll write: to understand the result fully. The meaning is the same, and we meet your style.
scenes.say_uz: Muharrir: Uchinchi qatorda infinitivni ajratibsiz. Yozuvchi: To fully understand aniqroq. Muharrir: Xato emas, lekin jurnal uslubi buni yoqtirmaydi, qayta yozing. Yozuvchi: Mayli. To understand the result fully deb yozaman. Ma’no bir xil, uslubga ham mos.

scenes.title: Nima uchun kelishdilar?
board: 1) Does the editor say it is wrong?
2) What is the reason to change it?
3) How does the writer fix it?
scenes.say_native: Uchta savol. Birinchi: muharrir ayrilgan infinitiv xato, deydimi? Ikkinchi: u nima uchun qayta yozishni so‘raydi? Uchinchi: yozuvchi jumlani qanday o‘zgartiradi? Javob berayotganda preskriptiv va deskriptiv tushunchalarini ishlating.
scenes.say: One: Does the editor say it is wrong? Two: Why does he ask for a change? Three: How does the writer rephrase it?
scenes.say_uz: Bir: Muharrir buni xato deydimi? Ikki: Nima uchun o‘zgartirishni so‘raydi? Uch: Yozuvchi uni qanday qayta yozadi?

scenes.title: Dialog javoblari
board: 1) No — he agrees it is not wrong
scenes.say_native: Birinchi: yo‘q, muharrir uni xato demaydi, bu deskriptiv yondashuv. Ikkinchi: jurnalning o‘z uslub qoidasi bor, bu preskriptiv talab, va u o‘quvchi hamda vaziyatga bog‘liq. Uchinchi: yozuvchi ravishni oxirga ko‘chiradi: ‘to understand the result fully’. Ko‘rdingizmi, professional yozuvchi qoida bilan kurashmaydi, balki uni vaziyatga qarab ishlatadi.
scenes.say: One: no, he agrees it is not wrong. Two: the journal's house style requires it. Three: to understand the result fully. A professional writer does not fight a convention but adapts to the context.
scenes.say_uz: Bir: yo‘q, xato demaydi. Ikki: jurnal uslubi. Uch: to understand the result fully. Professional yozuvchi qoida bilan kurashmaydi, vaziyatga moslashadi.

scenes.title: Tabiiy nutq: zaif shakllar
board: linking: pick it up → /pɪk ɪt ʌp/
scenes.say_native: Tabiiy nutqda ‘have’ zaiflashadi: ‘should have’ ‘should’ve’ bo‘lib eshitiladi, ‘shud-əv’. Aynan shu tovush tufayli ko‘plar ‘should of’ deb yozadi. Bu keng tarqalgan yozma xato, to‘g‘risi ‘should have’. Yana bir xususiyat: so‘zlar bir-biriga ulanadi. ‘Pick it up’ — ‘pi-ki-tap’ kabi eshitiladi. Ularni tanib olish tinglash uchun, to‘g‘ri yozish esa imlo uchun muhim.
scenes.say: In natural speech have becomes weak: should have sounds like should've, shud-uhv. That is why many people write should of, a very common spelling error. Words also link together: pick it up sounds like pi-ki-tup.
scenes.say_uz: Tabiiy nutqda have zaiflashadi: should've. Shu sababli should of degan imlo xatosi bor. So‘zlar ham ulanadi: pick it up — pi-ki-tap.

scenes.title: Ovoz chiqarib ayting
scenes.say_native: Uchta gapni zaif shakl bilan ayting. ‘Have’ so‘zini ‘haev’ deb to‘liq talaffuz qilmang, uni qisqa ‘əv’ ga aylantiring. Asosiy urg‘u ‘called’, ‘worse’ va ‘missed’ so‘zlarida bo‘lsin. Sekin boshlang, so‘ng tezlashtiring.
scenes.say: I should've called her. It could've been worse. He must've missed the train.
scenes.say_uz: Unga qo‘ng‘iroq qilishim kerak edi. Bundan battar bo‘lishi mumkin edi. U poyezdga kechikkan bo‘lsa kerak.

scenes.title: Talaffuz izohi
scenes.say_native: Yaxshi. Zaif shakllarda urg‘u mazmunli so‘zlarga tushadi: ‘called’, ‘worse’, ‘missed’. ‘Should’ve’ ham, ‘could’ve’ ham, ‘must’ve’ ham o‘tmish haqida taxmin yoki afsus bildiradi. ‘Must have missed’ — kechikkan bo‘lsa kerak, katta ishonch bilan. Agar siz hali ‘have’ ni to‘liq aytayotgan bo‘lsangiz, hech qisi yo‘q, faqat tinglaganingizda zaif shakl sizni adashtirmasin.
scenes.say: Good. Stress falls on the content words: called, worse, missed. Should've, could've and must've all look back at the past, expressing regret or deduction. Must have missed means I am fairly sure he missed it.
scenes.say_uz: Urg‘u mazmunli so‘zlarda. Should've, could've, must've o‘tmishga qaraydi: afsus yoki taxmin. Must have missed — kechikkan bo‘lsa kerak.

scenes.title: Sizning navbatingiz: uchta farq
scenes.say_native: Endi mustaqil vazifa. Bugungi mavzulardan uchta farqni tanlang va har birini ayting: avval qoida, keyin ma’no farqi, keyin o‘zingizning misolingiz. Masalan, ‘few’ va ‘a few’, ‘has been’ va ‘has gone’, yoki ‘stop to’ va ‘stop -ing’. Bir daqiqa gapiring, ovoz chiqarib.
scenes.say: Choose three contrasts from today's lesson. For each one, state the rule, explain the difference in meaning, and give your own example. You have sixty seconds.
scenes.say_uz: Bugungi darsdan uchta farqni tanlang. Har biri uchun qoidani ayting, ma’no farqini tushuntiring va o‘z misolingizni keltiring. Sizda oltmish soniya bor.

scenes.title: Namuna javob
board: has been / has gone — qaytgan / hali u yerda

examples.t: Few people came, but a few stayed.
examples.uz: Deyarli hech kim kelmadi, lekin bir necha kishi qoldi.

scenes.say_native: Namuna. Birinchi farq: ‘few’ salbiy, ‘a few’ ijobiy: ‘Few came, but a few stayed.’ Ikkinchi: ‘has been to’ — borib qaytgan, ‘has gone to’ — hali u yerda. Uchinchi: ‘stop to talk’ — gapirish uchun to‘xtamoq, ‘stop talking’ — gapirishni tugatmoq. Sizning javobingiz boshqa misollar bilan bo‘lishi mumkin, muhimi tuzilishi: qoida, ma’no, misol.
scenes.say: Here is a model. Few is negative, a few is positive. Has been to means he returned, has gone to means he is still there. Stop to talk gives a purpose, stop talking ends it. Your examples may differ, but the order of rule, meaning and example is the key.
scenes.say_uz: Namuna: few — salbiy, a few — ijobiy. Has been to — qaytgan, has gone to — hali u yerda. Stop to — maqsad, stop -ing — tugatish. Tuzilish: qoida, ma’no, misol.

scenes.title: Bugun nimani o‘rgandik
scenes.say_native: Qisqacha takrorlaymiz. Birinchi: istisnolarning mantig‘i bor, masalan, ‘be’ ning davomiy shakli va ‘news’ ning birligi. Ikkinchi: kichik farqlar ma’noni o‘zgartiradi: ‘remember to’ va ‘remember -ing’, ‘few’ va ‘a few’, urg‘u. Uchinchi: Britaniya va Amerika variantlari ikkalasi ham to‘g‘ri. To‘rtinchi: preskriptiv va deskriptiv yondashuvlarni vaziyatga qarab ishlating.
scenes.say: Let's recap. Exceptions have logic. Small words change meaning. Variation between varieties is normal. And in the end appropriate beats absolutely correct.
scenes.say_uz: Takrorlaymiz: istisnolarning mantig‘i bor. Kichik so‘zlar ma’noni o‘zgartiradi. Variantlar oddiy hol. Oxir-oqibat o‘rinli to‘g‘ridan ustun.

scenes.title: Uy vazifasi
scenes.say_native: Uy vazifasi: bugungi darsdan va o‘zingiz bilgan boshqa mavzulardan sakkizta nozik grammatik farqni tanlang va har birini yozma yoki og‘zaki tushuntiring. Har bir tushuntirishda qoida, ma’no farqi va kamida bitta o‘z misolingiz bo‘lsin. Muvaffaqiyat mezoni: sakkiztasi ham to‘liq va xatosiz. Keyingi darsda diplomatik til va yumshatish vositalarini o‘rganamiz.
scenes.say: Your homework is to explain eight subtle grammar contrasts. For each one give the rule, the difference in meaning and an example of your own. See you in the next lesson, where we study diplomatic language.
scenes.say_uz: Uy vazifasi: sakkizta nozik grammatik farqni tushuntiring. Har biri uchun qoida, ma’no farqi va o‘z misolingiz bo‘lsin. Keyingi darsda diplomatik tilni o‘rganamiz.

homework_uz: Bugungi darsdan va o‘zingiz bilgan boshqa mavzulardan sakkizta nozik grammatik farqni tanlang. Har birini qoida, ma’no farqi va kamida bitta o‘z misolingiz bilan yozma yoki og‘zaki tushuntiring. Muvaffaqiyat mezoni: sakkiztasi ham to‘liq va xatosiz.

quiz.q: Which sentence describes temporary, unusual behaviour?
quiz.why_uz: ‘is being’ vaqtincha, odatdagidan farqli xulqni bildiradi; ‘is rude’ esa xarakter.
News ‘s’ bilan tugasa ham birlik; o‘zbekcha ‘xabarlar’ ta’siri bilan ko‘plik xatosi qilinadi.

quiz.q: What does ‘I remember locking the door’ mean?
quiz.why_uz: Remember + -ing — o‘tmishdagi harakat xotirasi; remember to — vazifani bajarish.

quiz.q: Which sentence is positive in tone?
quiz.why_uz: ‘A few’ — bir necha, ijobiy; ‘few’ esa deyarli yo‘q degani.
Has gone to — hozir o‘sha yerda; has been to — borib qaytgan.

quiz.q: Which is the standard form after a preposition?
Why do many people wrongly write ‘should of’?
options: It is a regional grammar rule.
Of replaces have in formal English.
quiz.why_uz: Zaif ‘have’ /əv/ tovushi ‘of’ ga o‘xshaydi; to‘g‘risi should have.
Deskriptiv yondashuv haqiqiy ishlatilishni yozib boradi.

quiz.q: Which verb normally does NOT take the continuous form?
quiz.why_uz: Belong holat fe’li va davomiy bo‘lmaydi; boshqalar ma’noga qarab davomiy bo‘ladi.
